questions: Check signatory adoption, contract revision races and invalidation of completed tasks.
Bound registry loading and evidence required to reopen a consumer.
decision: Keep a small versioned pattern registry with conditional writes and precise consumer invalidation; distinguish semantic changes from formatting edits.
code_observations: patternctl already represents explicit signatories and pattern revisions; pattern_runner_contract integrates them into execution.
Shared normative patterns and runtime learnings are different contracts. Reopening every completed task would erase the selectivity the existing mechanism is intended to provide.
implementation_steps: Require the updater to provide the observed revision/digest and reject a stale writer rather than silently overwriting a newer contract.
Bind each consumer acceptance to the exact pattern revision. A revision change reopens only completed signatories that used an older revision; pending consumers just read the new revision.
Record a concise change rationale and migration impact. Avoid copying whole prior pattern histories into worker prompts.
Serialize writes for shared pattern files or use a tested lock/atomic write seam. Do not claim atomicity across independent files without recovery tests.
Limit registry lookup to assigned pattern IDs and make adoption evidence part of deterministic validation.
Require an expected canonical digest and serialize writes using the lifecycle ownership contract.
Separate formatting-only changes from semantic revisions; only changed normative contracts reopen stale accepted signatories.
Deliver the current pattern and bounded delta, not its full revision history, to each assigned consumer.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Two writers using the same starting revision cannot both silently succeed.
An unaffected completed task remains completed after an unrelated pattern change.
A stale completed signatory is reopened exactly once with a reason.
Malformed or escaping pattern paths cannot be read or deleted.
A worker receives only assigned current contracts, not the entire registry/history.
Two writers with the same starting digest cannot both overwrite the registry.
A formatting-only change does not reopen completed consumers.
A semantic revision reopens exactly its stale signatories and preserves their prior evidence as history.

alternatives.title: Copy rules into every task
alternatives.tradeoff: No registry; Drift and repeated tokens. Reject for evolving contracts

alternatives.title: Global pattern history in every prompt
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy visibility; Unbounded context and false invalidation. Reject

alternatives.title: CAS-style revision and signatories
alternatives.tradeoff: Minimal selective invalidation; Requires conflict/recovery tests. Recommended

alternatives.title: Distributed schema registry
alternatives.tradeoff: Strong external governance; Unneeded service and migration cost. Defer

cost_model: Measure number of reopened tasks and repeated context bytes per real contract change. Selective invalidation saves only when the consumer mapping is accurate; missing signatories is a correctness defect.
unverified: Cross-host concurrent execution requires an explicit storage/locking contract; local filesystem tests cannot establish distributed locking.
Hash equality proves canonical bytes, not semantic equivalence unless the canonical contract format is defined and tested.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Strengthen versioned shared patterns with compare-and-swap updates and selective consumer invalidation, without building a global context dump.
revision_delta: The revision adds semantic-change classification, a single-writer boundary and a bounded pattern delta, avoiding unnecessary reopen cascades from formatting-only changes.
decision_analysis: Patterns are contracts, not a shared scratchpad. The expected digest/revision must accompany an update so a stale worker cannot silently overwrite another decision. Write under the same ownership/lock discipline as lifecycle state; a second ad-hoc locking convention would create deadlocks and incompatible recovery.

A semantic contract change reopens accepted signatories on an older revision. A formatting edit that leaves the canonical contract unchanged should not trigger code reimplementation. Preserve a canonical representation or explicitly classify the revision and test that classification; do not let an unverified model claim decide it alone.

Pending consumers read the current contract. Completed consumers retain the exact adopted revision and evidence. Bound the change note to the normative delta, affected consumers and migration test. Sending the complete history to every worker defeats selective loading.

The Kubernetes source supplies an optimistic concurrency example, not a mandate to run a cluster. A plain local registry with hashes, lock and generation-aware writes is the least disruptive implementation. Use formal schema or interface tests where possible to decide whether a consumer is actually stale.
ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.
baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
